authors: Hyewon Choi;Yooinn Hong;Jiao Wang
title: National-scale PM2.5 health consequences of a proposed LNG power project in South Korea: looking beyond localized assessment boundaries
abstract: Environmental impact assessments (EIAs) in South Korea rely heavily on localized dispersion models within restricted geographical boundaries (∼10 km), failing to capture regional secondary PM2.5 formation and broad population exposure. To address these limitations, this study pursues two distinct objectives: (1) evaluating systemic deficiencies in the current EIA framework, and (2) quantifying the nationwide health impacts and monetized mortality damages of a proposed 3 GW liquefied natural gas power cluster at the Yongin Semiconductor Industrial Complex. We employed Global InMAP—selected specifically for its ability to simulate long-range atmospheric transport and secondary PM2.5 chemistry across national scales where local models fail—under 35%, 55%, and 75% capacity factor (CF) scenarios. Health outcomes were modeled nationwide and monetized using domestic and international Values of a Statistical Life. Regarding health impact quantification, the proposed cluster is projected to cause 21.5–31.1 additional annual premature deaths nationwide, with secondary PM2.5 driving 63%–71% of this burden. Under the central 55% CF scenario, annual monetized mortality damages range from 34.4 billion KRW (∼USD 23 million; domestic benchmark) to 195.9–295.5 billion KRW (∼USD 143–201 million; international benchmarks). Regarding EIA framework evaluation, spatial disaggregation revealed critical regulatory blind spots: only 14%–16% of attributable premature deaths occur within the typical 10 km EIA assessment radius, while 67%–69% fall outside Yongin City and 46%–47% outside host Gyeonggi Province. Geographically bounded EIAs omit the vast majority of health externalities; regulatory frameworks must integrate regional secondary PM2.5 modeling and transparently monetize health damages in energy planning decisions.

authors: Kai Yang;Jinghua Chen;Tianliang Zhao;Xiangde Xu;Chunsong Lu;Shizuo Fu;Yuehan Luo;Qingjian Yang;Ziqian Liu;Zhikuan Li;Lin Wu;Yuxiang Jin
title: Lake-Mountain synergy in convective  clouds and precipitation over the Tibetan  Plateau: a large-eddy simulation study
abstract:
The Tibetan Plateau has little available moisture and energy, so convection is hard to develop. Large-eddy simulations indicates the lake promotes low-level moistening and lowers the barrier to convective initiation, produces shallow clouds and week rain. Mountain alone force lifting, yet the lack of moisture limits terrain-driven precipitation. Lake-mountain coupling is key: the mountain lifts lake-supplied moisture but also block low-level moisture transport, reshaping precipitation patterns. 
 Idealized large-eddy simulations (LES) are used to examine lake-mountain effects on clouds and precipitation over the Tibetan Plateau (TP) under conditions of low air density and limited moisture. This study conducts LES respectively with lake-only, mountain-only, and combined lake-mountain configurations. The alpine lake alleviates key constraints on convective organization by enhancing low-level moisture and reducing thermodynamic inhibition to convective initiation. However, in this energy- and moisture-limited environment, the lake alone induces only shallow ascent, sustaining shallow convection and weak precipitation with limited deepening. By contrast, mountain alone provides mechanically forced uplift, but the overall scarcity of moisture over the TP confines precipitation to a narrow area near the mountain. With combined lake-mountain configurations, lake-supplied moisture is lifted by the downstream mountain, deep convective clouds develop, yielding strong and extensive precipitation. Notably, mountains exhibit a reversed role in lake-mountain interactions affecting clouds and precipitation processes, owing to the competition between orographic lifting and blocking effects. High mountains enhance precipitation on the upstream side while suppressing downstream development by restricting low-level moisture transport from lake source, whereas low mountains allow broader horizontal moisture advection but induce weaker vertical development. Overall, lake-mountain coupling is intrinsic to the TP's high-elevation, moisture and energy limited environment, where lake-driven moistening lowers initiation barriers, orographic lifting and blocking organize and deepen convection, and mixed-phase processes further reshape precipitation patterns. This pathway is typically not dominant over the low-elevation regions. These findings clarify how high-elevation surface heterogeneity affects clouds and precipitation, with implications for the Asian water cycle.

authors: Seethala Chellappan;David Painemal;Mandana Thieman;Christian Pelayo;William L. Smith Jr.;Lynn M. Russell
title: Spring-summer atmospheric circulation and boundary layer processes modulating aerosol and cloud characteristics over the coastal Northeast Pacific during EPCAPE
abstract:
We analyzed observations from the ARM (Atmospheric Radiation Measurement) EPCAPE (Eastern Pacific Cloud Aerosol Precipitation Experiment) campaign at coastal California, and satellite cloud properties to understand how large-scale weather patterns influence marine low clouds and aerosols. Using ERA5 data and Self-Organizing Maps, we identified nine synoptic regimes linked to cloud cover, depth, and liquid water path. Satellite data show anticyclone position strongly affects cloud properties, while aerosol–cloud covariability depends on turbulence and supersaturation. 
 Observations collected during the ARM Eastern Pacific Cloud Aerosol Precipitation Experiment (EPCAPE) for the period spanning April to September 2023 (spring and summer) at Scripps Pier in La Jolla, California (32.8669° N, 117.2569° W) were used to investigate the regional-scale atmospheric factors that control the variability of predominant marine low clouds and aerosols in the coastal boundary layer. Using Self-Organizing Maps (SOMs) applied to ERA5 sea level pressure and near-surface wind fields, we classify the synoptic evolution of the subtropical anticyclone into 9 regimes. This regime categorization highlights the following dominant features in Northeast Pacific: (1) regimes that capture the evolution of the anticyclone in terms of magnitude (strong vs. weak) and location (coastal vs. offshore), with their corresponding transitions in boundary layer wind strengthening and large-scale subsidence (regimes: 1–3 vs. 6–8), (2) a second dominant feature  characterized by an anticyclone with its core at the northwestern edge of the domain, resulting in modest sea level pressure changes near Scripps Pier (regimes 6–8), (3) patterns with a weakened subtropical anticyclone south of Scripps Pier and a midlatitude cyclone further north (regimes 4 and 5), and (4) an additional regime that captures anomalies that minimally depart from the climatological mean (regime 9). GOES-18 satellite cloud retrievals reveal that regimes associated with an anticyclone core closer to the EPCAPE coastal site (regimes 1–4) is associated with reduced low-cloud fraction, shallower clouds, and low liquid water path (LWP) along the shoreline; whereas regimes with a west/north-westward-displaced anticyclone combined with a weak coastal inland low-pressure feature (regimes 6–8) that support extensive stratocumulus with higher LWP and elevated cloud tops. Variability in the aerosol distribution is also controlled by the synoptic scale processes. Regimes with a relatively weak anticyclone centered adjacent to the Scripps Pier (regime 4) generally feature the highest concentrations of particles with diameter  ≤ 0.1 µm, associated with a stable boundary layer and stagnation under weak winds. Regimes with anticyclone strengthening farther offshore (regimes 6–8) have relatively lower aerosol concentrations. The partial inconsistency in the evolution of the cloud droplet number concentration (Nd) and aerosol concentration indicates that the variability in boundary layer turbulence is a critical component that explains the aerosol activation into Nd.

authors: Yuxuan Lu;Ruonan Wang;Ningning Zhang;Qiyuan Wang;Yuepeng Pan;Qian Jiang;Xuexi Tie
title: Impacts of the heterogeneous ammonia uptake  on air quality in the North China Plain
abstract:
This study explored how ammonia reacts with secondary organic aerosols over northern China using model simulations constrained by observational data. The reaction had little effect on overall fine particle pollution but  may provide an additional source of nitrogen-containing organic particles, improving understanding of atmospheric pollution formation and chemical processes in air quality models. 
 Previous studies have revealed that the heterogeneous uptake of ammonia (NH3) on secondary organic aerosols (SOA) may influence the NH3 budget, nitrate aerosol chemistry, and the regional PM2.5 burden, also constituting an important source of nitrogen-containing organic compounds (NOCs). However, regional modeling remains hindered by large uncertainties in the uptake coefficient (γ) and limited field-based constraints. In this study, we incorporate a first-order NOCs-forming NH3–SOA reactive-uptake pathway into WRF-Chem and adopt a literature-based sensitivity range of γ=10-5-10-3 to evaluate its impacts on air quality and particulate organic nitrogen over the North China Plain during November 2017. Laboratory evidence of declining reaction efficiency and comparison with the measured NOCs burden support considering γ=10-5 as a conservative upper limit for sustained operation of this pathway under the conditions examined. With γ=10-5, the uptake reaction decreases NH3 concentrations by 0.62 % and inorganic aerosol and PM2.5 concentrations by less than 0.06 %, while producing 1.2 µg m−3 of NOCs in the NCP. These results indicate that the pathway has only a minor influence on NH3 and PM2.5 under the present conditions, but may provide an additional source of particulate organic nitrogen.

explanation: 该论文研究了中国地表臭氧污染的变化，结合气象学方法和机器学习技术，分析气象因素对臭氧浓度的影响。这与大气环境遥感技术中的空气质量监测、气象影响分析等方向密切相关。
authors: Zhenying Ye;Run Liu;Tingting Hu;Guoxin Chen;Min Wu
title: Meteorological normalization of surface ozone variability across warm and cold seasons in China during 2015–2024
abstract:
Surface ozone pollution in China keeps rising despite cleaner primary emissions. We used national observations from 2015 to 2024 and machine learning to separate weather effects from longer-term changes. Ozone increased in both warm and cold seasons, and recent unfavorable weather further worsened pollution, suggesting that future control plans should consider seasonal and regional differences. 
 Surface ozone (O3) concentrations in China have continued to increase, but the roles of meteorological variability and longer-term changes remain uncertain, particularly across seasons and regions. Here, we combined LightGBM-based meteorological normalization with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) to investigate warm- and cold-season variations in maximum daily 8 h average O3 (MDA8  O3) across China during 2015–2024. The models reproduced daily MDA8  O3 variability reasonably well, with mean testing R2 values of 0.62 and 0.68 in the warm and cold seasons, respectively. Observed national mean MDA8  O3 increased by 2.0 and 2.2 µgm-3yr-1 in the two seasons, respectively. After meteorological normalization, the corresponding trends were 1.1 and 1.2 µgm-3yr-1, indicating that meteorological variability alone cannot fully explain the observed increases. The normalized long-term component may reflect changes in precursor emissions, background O3, regional transport, and other processes not explicitly represented in the model. SHAP analysis revealed distinct seasonal and regional meteorological associations. During the warm season, temperature and solar radiation were more important in northern inland and basin regions, whereas relative humidity and wind were more important in southern coastal regions. During the cold season, solar radiation dominated across most regions, while relative humidity was more important in the Pearl River Delta. Meteorological contributions generally shifted from negative during 2015–2019 to positive after 2019, amplifying O3 pollution in several regions. These findings highlight the importance of accounting for seasonal meteorological variability when evaluating long-term O3 trends in China.

explanation: 该论文评估了GOSAT/GOSAT-2卫星的XCO2代理XCH4产品，通过与TCCON地面观测站的比较，研究了中国地区的甲烷浓度监测。这直接涉及大气环境遥感技术，特别是卫星观测和大气成分分析。
authors: Xinran Jiang;Gerrit de Leeuw;Cheng Fan;Jeon-Teo Dong;Andrew Gerald Barr;Wei Wang;Minqiang Zhou;Zhengqiang Li
title: Evaluation of the GOSAT/GOSAT-2 XCO2 proxy XCH4 product by comparison with TCCON observations over China
abstract:
Evaluation of satellite greenhouse gas data is crucial for climate monitoring and mitigation. We assessed four XCO2 Proxy XCH4 results using Hefei and Xianghe Total Carbon Column Observing Network (TCCON) sites in China. We found that the accuracy of retrieval products varies between both sites. Fundamental assumption of Proxy method leaves uncertainties. Independent XCO2 proxy comparison with TCCON data show discrepancies requiring continuous evaluation for proper determination of XCH4. 
 Methane (CH4) is the second most important well-mixed greenhouse gas after carbon dioxide (CO2) and its accurate monitoring supports China's “dual carbon” goals. Satellites enable global CH4 monitoring using various sensors and retrieval techniques. The XCO2 proxy method derives the column-averaged dry-air mole fraction of CH4 (XCH4) from the XCH4/XCO2 ratio and an independent XCO2 estimate, exploiting the overlapping absorption bands of CH4 and CO2 near 1.6 µm and assuming similar vertical distributions to reduce common retrieval errors. In this study, four XCO2 proxy methane products, GOSAT SRPR, OCPR, FOCAL Proxy, and GOSAT-2 SRPR, are evaluated using Total Carbon Column Observing Network (TCCON) ground-based observations at the Hefei and Xianghe sites in China. GOSAT products show lower bias and RMSE at Xianghe than at Hefei, while GOSAT-2 products are similar at both sites, with lower bias, RMSE, and standard deviation compared with the GOSAT products and approximately 51 % of retrievals meeting GCOS requirements. All products, except OCPR, overestimate XCH4 at Hefei and underestimate XCH4 at Xianghe, due to XCO2 model errors and spatial differences associated with regional and local methane emissions affecting both sites. Furthermore, the overestimation of the ratio implies that the fundamental assumption of the XCO2 proxy method is not fulfilled, primarily due to systematic positive biases in the satellite-retrieved XCH4 used in the proxy calculation. This study provides key error characteristics and spatial-seasonal biases in current satellite proxy methane products over China, supporting future retrieval optimization.

authors: Cong Cao;Wei Chen;Xu Yu;Wing Hei Marco Wong;Ningning Sun;Kun Zhang;Weicong Cheng;Jianping Gan;Jian Zhen Yu
title: Comparative nitrogen speciation in marine and coastal urban aerosols of the Greater Bay Area and implications for PM2.5-bound nitrogen deposition
abstract:
Coastal waters receive nitrogen from the air, but its chemical forms are poorly understood. We sampled airborne particles during a cruise in the Guangdong–Hong Kong–Macau Greater Bay Area and at an urban site in Hong Kong. Nitrogen chemistry differed between urban and marine air, and carbon-containing nitrogen declined offshore. Fine particles supplied nitrogen to coastal waters, highlighting the need to consider its chemical form when assessing nutrient inputs and potential ecosystem effects. 
 We present a summer 2024 comparative study of aerosol nitrogen speciation in the Guangdong–Hong Kong–Macau Greater Bay Area (GBA), examining how nitrogen abundance and chemical composition vary between coastal urban air and adjacent marine air, and their implications for nitrogen deposition. Concurrent shipboard and urban observations from 12 July to 3 August 2024 included bulk inorganic nitrogen (IN) and organic nitrogen (ON) measurements in PM2.5 and offline aerosol mass spectrometry (AMS) of water extracts. Regional mean PM2.5-bound total nitrogen and IN concentrations increased from western to eastern coastal waters, reflecting both spatial and temporal variability. Bulk PM2.5-bound ON concentrations decreased offshore by 12.2 % per 10 km, with estimates ranging from 10.1 % to 14.2 % across sensitivity analyses. Beyond these concentration patterns, AMS mass spectra revealed contrasting nitrogen chemistry. Water extracts of urban PM2.5 exhibited higher NO+/NO2+ ratios than marine PM2.5 extracts (7.9 ±  2.6 versus 5.4 ± 1.2) and more pronounced organic nitrate-related fragments. These complementary signatures indicate more prominent organic-nitrate-related oxidized-N functionality in urban PM2.5, consistent with NOx–VOC photochemistry at the urban site. Four ship-influenced samples showed enhanced imidazole-like fragment signatures, identifying an additional compositional feature warranting targeted investigation. Estimated PM2.5-bound nitrogen dry-deposition fluxes were 0.036 and 0.040 mg N m−2 d−1 for marine and coastal urban environments, respectively, with overlapping model-sensitivity ranges. These results demonstrate a notable coastal transition in nitrogen chemical form and suggest that ON speciation should be considered when modelling nitrogen deposition to coastal waters and assessing potential ecosystem responses.

explanation: 该论文研究了氡示踪法（Radon Tracer Method）用于估算温室气体排放的方法，涉及大气成分分析和排放监测，与大气环境遥感技术中的气体成分分析和排放估算相关。
authors: Scott D. Chambers;Ute Karstens;Alan D. Griffiths;Stefan Röttger;Arnoud Frumau;Christopher T. Roulston;Peter Sperlich;Felix Vogel;Agnieszka Podstawczyńska;Dafina Kikaj;Maksym Gachkivskyi;Michel Ramonet;Blagoj Mitrevski;Janja Vaupotič;Xuemeng Chen;Annette Röttger
title: Review of the Radon Tracer Method for GHG emission estimates: development, application guidelines, improvements, and caveats
abstract:
The Radon Tracer Method (RTM) is a top-down approach to estimate greenhouse gas emissions. While simple in principle, incorrect use can complicate interpretation of results. Based on observations from a range of contrasting sites, this article reviews the underlying assumptions and key considerations for applying the RTM. It also introduces the concept of coupling RTM analyses with nocturnal stability classification, to reduce uncertainty of fetch estimates and improve interpretation of results. 
 The Radon Tracer Method (RTM) is an established, independent top-down method that can be used to cross-check bottom-up greenhouse gas (GHG) emission estimates. Furthermore, as uncertainties of Atmospheric Transport Models are reduced, the RTM can provide a convenient means of quantifying continual improvement of inversion-based top-down GHG emission estimates. While the accessibility and perceived simplicity of the RTM drive its popularity, the technique is better suited to assessing long-term relative changes in GHG emissions than absolute changes, due to short-term soil moisture influences on simulated radon flux uncertainty. Considerations for applying the RTM, based on fundamental assumptions of the technique's development, are application and season specific, making the development of a “standard protocol” for its use challenging. After proposing a novel alternative means of applying the nocturnal accumulation RTM, which improves interpretation of findings, we use measurements from a range of contrasting sites to discuss the significance of the technique's eight key considerations: (i) nocturnal window definition, (ii) radon and target gas accumulation thresholds, (iii) radon-to-target gas regression linearity thresholds, (iv) measurement height, (v) the contributing fetch, (vi) spatial and temporal radon flux variability, (vii) RTM temporal resolution, and (viii) application specific selection of a suitable radon monitor. The insight provided by these examples to the flexibility (or otherwise) of the technique's considerations will clarify the implications if users choose to relax or ignore them, potentially making future RTM studies more directly comparable.

explanation: 该研究涉及全球卫星导航系统（GNSS）无线电 occultation 数据，这是一种用于天气预报的重要数据来源。研究分析了 12 个 GNSS occultation 星座的观测特征和覆盖范围互补性，涉及卫星观测、空间覆盖和时间覆盖等，这与大气环境遥感技术（如卫星观测、大气成分分析）密切相关。
authors: Wenqiang Lu;Ran Chen;Na Xu;Xiangguang Meng;Lei Xue;Mi Liao;Yan Liu;Peng Guo;Guanglin Yang;Xiuqing Hu;Xiangang Zhao;Yueqiang Sun
title: Global sampling characteristics and coverage complementarity of 12 GNSS radio occultation constellations
abstract:
Global satellite navigation system occultation data is one of the important sources for weather forecasting. As more and more occultation missions are launched, it's becoming really important to understand how these constellations work together. This study found that combining data from 12 constellations greatly increases time and space coverage, but some missions are still essential for observing tropical regions. These findings provide guidance for future satellite planning. 
 This study analyzes observations from COSMIC-2, FY-3, GRACE-C/D, KOMPSAT-5, MetOp-B/C, PAZ, PlanetiQ, Sentinel-6A, Spire, TerraSAR-X/TanDEM-X, TM-1, and YY-1 collected during 1–7 January 2026 to compare their spatial distributions, grid-cell occupancy, area-weighted surface coverage, and local-time sampling; quantify the sampling gains achieved through multi-mission integration; and assess changes in sampling when COSMIC-2 is excluded. The results show that orbital configuration determines latitudinal and local-time sampling, whereas event abundance and constellation size primarily control grid coverage. Large constellations such as YY-1 and TM-1 provide the strongest global continuity, while missions with different orbital inclinations offer complementary sampling across latitude bands. Combining all missions substantially reduces spatial gaps and provides area-weighted global surface coverage of 99.71 % and 99.99 % at 1.0 and 2.0° resolutions,respectively. Within 6 h windows, the mean area-weighted joint coverage reaches 76.79 % at 2.0° resolution. Multi-mission integration also broadens local-time cycle. Excluding COSMIC-2 reduces the number of RO events within 5° S–5° N by 21.75 %, although the remaining 11 missions retain most of the mid- and high-latitude sampling. These results characterize the sampling complementarity and resilience of the multi-mission observing system.

explanation: 该论文与大气环境遥感技术密切相关，因为它利用GRACE卫星的重力测量技术来监测地下水位变化，这是一种遥感技术。此外，论文还提到了大气水循环和气候变化对地下水的影响，这与大气环境遥感监测密切相关。
authors: Andreas Güntner;Ehsan Sharifi;Julian Haas;Eva Boergens;Feifei Cao;Christoph Dahle;Neda Darbeheshti;Henryk Dobslaw;Inés Dussaillant;Wouter Dorigo;Frank Flechtner;Adrian Jäggi;Miriam Kosmale;Martin Lasser;Kari Luojus;Ulrich Meyer;Adam Pasik;Wolfgang Preimesberger;Claudia Ruz Vargas;Michael Zemp
title: The Global Gravity-based Groundwater Product (G3P)
abstract:
We provide a data set that illustrates how the amount of water that is stored in the subsurface as groundwater varies in time over the continents of the Earth. An important part of the data comes from satellites that track changes in water by its gravity effect. The data allow for assessing how groundwater as the most important freshwater resource for mankind and ecosystems is affected by climate variability, climate change and withdrawal by human activities. 
 Groundwater is one of the most important freshwater resources for ecosystems and mankind. Because of its fundamental role in the Earth's water and energy cycles, groundwater has been declared an essential climate variable by GCOS, the Global Climate Observing System. Similar to other subsurface states and fluxes, groundwater is difficult to monitor at the global scale, with sufficient spatial coverage and over climate-relevant time scales. The Global Gravity-based Groundwater Product (G3P) is a global observation-based data set of large-scale groundwater storage variations. G3P capitalizes on the unique capability of GRACE and GRACE-FO satellite gravimetry as the only remote sensing technology to monitor subsurface mass variations. In a mass balance approach, satellite-based, in situ observation-based and model-based water storage variations of snow water equivalent, root-zone soil moisture, glacier mass, and surface water storage are subtracted from GRACE/-FO terrestrial water storage anomalies to result in monthly variations of groundwater storage. For this combination, the individual compartmental storage data are spatially filtered to be consistent with the spatial resolution of terrestrial water storage from satellite gravimetry. The G3P data set presented here covers the period 2002 to 2023 with monthly resolution on a 0.5° global grid and includes propagated uncertainty information. We describe the details of the G3P data processing chain and of each contributing data stream including their uncertainties and limitations, provide examples of spatial and temporal groundwater storage variations represented by the G3P data set, and present exemplary evaluation results against in situ groundwater observations for three large aquifer systems. The latter show moderate to high temporal correlation of aquifer-average G3P groundwater storage and in situ groundwater level variations on seasonal and interannual time scales. G3P is a prototype for an operational global groundwater service, under development as a cross-cutting extension of the existing portfolio of the Copernicus Climate Change Service C3S. The G3P data set is available via GFZ Data Services at https://doi.org/10.5880/g3p.2024.001 (Güntner et al., 2024).

authors: Felipe Matus;Marcia Paredes;Miguel Lagos-Zúñiga;Alex Garcés;Diego Pinto;Germán Aguilar;Santiago Montserrat
title: Extreme precipitation events: a comprehensive  catalog for northern Chile (17.5° S to 30.0° S)
abstract:
We compiled a detailed catalog of extreme seasonal precipitation events observed in northern Chile during 1979–2019 to better understand how, when, and where these occur. The catalog uses atmospheric data and local meteorological products to identify different types of storms categories occurring in the study area, and the daily meteorological conditions for each event. This information was tested to evaluate landslide occurrence and composite analysis in Chilean arid and semiarid regions. 
 This study presents a comprehensive catalog of the most extreme seasonal rainfall events of northern Chile between 1979 and 2019. We analyzed its meteorological patterns across three latitudinal bands (17.5–23.5° S, 23.5–27° S, and 27–30° S) using daily precipitation and mean daily temperature from the CR2METv2.5 product, and vertically integrated water vapor transport data (IVT) from the ERA5 reanalysis. These events were classified into three main precipitation categories: Stratiform, Coast, and Andes Mountain. The Andes Mountain category was further subdivided into five subcategories based on IVT patterns and precipitation spatial distribution: North Andes, South Andes, Along Andes, Convergence, and Westerly IVT. In total, the catalog comprises 472 extreme precipitation events corresponding to 408 unique storm dates, each characterized by date, precipitation category, maximum precipitation within the latitudinal band, average storm temperature, and snow line elevation determined through empirical methods and remote sensing from daily MODIS imagery. The dataset is available as a CSV catalog with additional NetCDF files containing gridded precipitation, IVT, and MODIS snow cover fields for each event. To test the applicability of this catalog, we characterized extreme events composite results for the Austral summer between 27–30° S (latitudinal band 3), showing that events within each category yield coherent synoptic patterns. Additionally, we contrasted our catalog with an existing national landslide inventory of 548 events in the study area, finding that just six cataloged storms (all classified as Stratiform) account for 203 debris flow events (37 %), indicating the March 2015 and May 2017 storms were alone responsible for 168 of them. We also estimated the approximate debris flow volumes for the March 2015 Atacama event using a transport-capacity approach, showing reasonable agreement for deposits larger than 4000 m3. These findings enhance our understanding of extreme precipitation events in Chile and provide a valuable resource for storyline analysis and precipitation pattern identification. Catalog is available at Zenodo: https://doi.org/10.5281/ZENODO.14342935 (Matus et al., 2026).

explanation: 该论文研究的是全球海洋温度和盐度剖面数据集，整合了多平台的现场观测和卫星追踪的中小尺度涡旋观测，这与大气环境遥感技术相关，因为海洋温度和盐度是影响大气环流和空气质量的重要因素。论文中提到的涡旋追踪和海洋剖面数据对于研究气候变化和海洋-大气相互作用具有重要意义，这些都属于大气环境遥感技术的研究范畴。
topic_words: ['卫星观测', '海洋盐度', '温度剖面', '涡旋追踪', '空气质量监测']
authors: Qingyou He;Yunchen Liu;Weikang Zhan;Yinghui He;Zhenting Mo;Peiya Zhang;Shuqun Cai;Lijing Cheng;Haigang Zhan
title: A global eddy-collocated temperature and salinity profile dataset (v1.0): integrating multiplatform in situ observations with satellite-tracking mesoscale eddies
abstract:
We integrated nearly 30 years of global ocean temperature and salinity profile data with satellite mesoscale eddy observations, matching 5.46 million in-situ profiles to adjacent eddies. This dataset enables researchers to characterize the regional three-dimensional eddy structure and investigate how eddies modify ocean thermohaline distributions, alter stratification and mixing, trigger extreme events, drive heat and tracer transport, and respond to climate change. 
 Mesoscale eddies are ubiquitous rotating water masses with horizontal scales of tens to hundreds of kilometers that play a key role in redistributing heat and salt throughout the global ocean. However, the lack of long-term observational records has limited systematic assessments of their thermohaline effects from regional to global scales. Here, we present a global eddy-collocated temperature and salinity profile dataset spanning 29 years (1993–2021), constructed by integrating multiplatform in situ hydrographic observations with satellite-derived mesoscale eddy tracking products. The dataset contains 5.46 million quality-controlled temperature–salinity profiles, each collocated with its nearest mesoscale eddy and is publicly available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20607854 (He, 2026). The observations provide broad global coverage, with most 2° × 2° grid boxes containing more than 200 profiles, enabling statistically robust analyses of eddy-induced temperature and salinity anomalies. Validation against previously documented regional eddy signatures demonstrates that the dataset reliably captures characteristic temperature and salinity anomaly structures associated with eddies. Example applications demonstrate its utility for characterizing regional three-dimensional eddy thermohaline patterns, assessing global eddy effects on upper ocean stratification and subsurface temperature extremes, and providing an observational basis for estimating eddy-induced heat, salt, and water-mass transports. As a long-term observation-based eddy-collocated profile product, this dataset provides a valuable resource for studies of eddy impacts on ocean circulation, tracer redistribution, climate variability, and model evaluation.

explanation: 该论文研究的是利用物理感知深度学习重建亚洲关键热点地区的对流层二氧化氮（NO2）数据集，涉及卫星观测和空气质量监测，与大气环境遥感技术密切相关。
authors: Hongrui Gao;Qin He;Kai Qin;Jhoon Kim;Diego Loyola;Pravash Tiwari;Lingxiao Lu;Jason B. Cohen
title: A gapless 0.05° daytime-hourly tropospheric NO2 dataset (2019–2024) over key Asian hotspots reconstructed using physics-aware deep learning
abstract:
This study provides a continuous daytime-hourly tropospheric nitrogen dioxide dataset over four Asian pollution hotspots from 2019 to 2024, reconstructed using satellite observations, meteorological reanalysis, and physics-aware machine learning. The dataset fills observational gaps, captures fine-scale spatial and diurnal dynamics, and supports regional air-quality and health impact studies. 
 High-frequency observations of tropospheric nitrogen dioxide (NO2) support regional air quality assessment and analysis of its photochemical evolution. Although the Geostationary Environment Monitoring Spectrometer (GEMS) and other new-generation geostationary satellites provide hourly observations during daytime, their spatial coverage is often severely compromised by cloud obstruction and inherent retrieval limitations. Furthermore, their short observation history hinders long-term, cross-regional environmental assessments. To address this, this study presents a gapless, 0.05° daytime-hourly tropospheric NO2 vertical column density (VCD) dataset for representative hotspots in Asia spanning 2019 to 2024, reconstructed using a physics-aware deep learning framework. The framework integrates partial convolutions to handle irregularly missing satellite observations and proposes a Physics-aware Normalization (PhysNorm) module. Specifically, the model inputs comprise the 0.05° TROPOMI tropospheric NO2 VCD and its validity mask, together with 0.25° predictors including ERA5 meteorological variables, EAC4 total-column NO2, land cover, elevation, and the cosine of the solar zenith angle. The supervised training target is the hourly GEMS tropospheric NO2 VCD from 2023. PhysNorm dynamically modulates 0.05° high-resolution feature maps using 0.25° low-resolution physical features, thereby ensuring rigorous physical continuity while filling data gaps. Validation results show that the model performs exceptionally on the test set (R2= 0.889) and maintains high generalization stability in an independent validation on 2024 data, which was not used for training. Cross-validation against an independent polar-orbiting satellite instrument (GOME-2C) confirms the reliability of the dataset in reconstructing pollution hotspots and its applicability to periods without GEMS observations (2019–2022). Comparison with independent ground-based Pandora observations showed an overall correlation of R=0.644 for 2019–2024. Using this reconstructed dataset, this study finely delineates the periodic diurnal characteristics of NO2 in typical Asian regions and characterizes inter-annual variations in NO2 concentration patterns over the past six years. This newly generated dataset provides a spatiotemporally continuous daytime record, overcoming the limitations of cloud cover and short observational histories, thereby facilitating long-term, high-resolution air quality assessments and epidemiological studies. This dataset is available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20427767 (Gao et al., 2026).

explanation: 该研究涉及利用生态水动力学模拟系统和集合卡尔曼滤波数据同化系统开发的12年数据集，用于描述伊势湾的水动力和水质变化。虽然主要关注的是近海生态和水体化学变量（如溶解氧），但其使用了数据同化技术来提高对水下动态的表征，这与大气环境遥感技术在空气质量监测和水体成分分析中的应用有间接关联。
authors: Yoshitaka Matsuzaki;Hayato Mizuguchi;Tetsunori Inoue
title: Ise Bay Reanalysis (IBRA): a 12-year ecological hydrodynamic reanalysis dataset for Ise Bay, Japan
abstract:
We developed a 12-year dataset describing water movement and water quality in Ise Bay, Japan. Low oxygen levels in coastal waters can harm marine ecosystems, but observations alone cannot fully capture when and where these conditions occur. To address this problem, we combined simulations with measurements collected at monitoring stations. The resulting dataset reproduces seasonal changes and oxygen depletion in the bay and can support scientific research and environmental assessment. 
 Reanalysis datasets based on coupled ocean circulation and ecosystem models are essential tools for understanding coastal environmental variability and supporting water-quality management. However, the development of such datasets for semi-enclosed coastal systems remains limited, particularly for those incorporating subsurface biogeochemical observations such as dissolved oxygen (DO). This study presents the Ise Bay Reanalysis (IBRA), a high-resolution, 12-year (2011–2022) reanalysis dataset of hydrodynamic and biogeochemical variables for Ise Bay, Japan. The dataset was generated using the Ecological hydrodynamics simulation system of the Port and Airport Research Institute Simulator (EcoPARI-Simulator), coupled with an ensemble Kalman filter data assimilation system that assimilated in situ observations of water temperature, salinity, and bottom-layer DO at 6 h intervals. The resulting dataset has an hourly temporal resolution and resolves the entire water column. IBRA has three key distinguishing features. First, unlike many previous reanalysis datasets that rely primarily on satellite observations, IBRA assimilates continuous in situ measurements throughout the water column, including high-frequency DO observations, thereby improving the representation of subsurface dynamics. Second, the 6 h assimilation cycle enables the dataset to resolve short-term variability driven by tidal processes, which are a dominant control of coastal transport and mixing. Third, spatially coherent corrections are applied across the entire bay using an ensemble Kalman filter, ensuring spatial consistency in both physical and biogeochemical fields while avoiding artificial discontinuities often associated with simpler data assimilation approaches. The quality of IBRA was evaluated using statistical metrics and detailed comparisons against in situ observations. Data assimilation improved overall agreement with observations across multiple stations and depths, particularly for bottom-layer DO concentrations. The dataset successfully reproduced seasonal variability, vertical stratification, and the formation and persistence of hypoxic conditions in the inner bay, while also capturing well-oxygenated conditions near the bay mouth. Furthermore, the spatial distributions of temperature, salinity, and DO were realistically represented, including the intrusion of offshore water masses and associated horizontal gradients. The IBRA dataset therefore provides a dynamically consistent and comprehensive representation of physical and biogeochemical variability in a semi-enclosed coastal system. It is expected to serve as a valuable resource for studies of coastal hypoxia, water-quality assessment, and environmental management. The IBRA dataset is publicly available via Zenodo at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19808667 (Matsuzaki et al., 2026).

explanation: 该论文主要关注海洋物种的栖息地变化和适宜性，虽然涉及海洋环境，但并未直接涉及大气环境遥感技术，如空气质量监测、卫星观测、大气成分分析或气溶胶反演等。
authors: Yixuan Li;Shijun Zheng;Le Yu;Zhenrong Du;Fanghua Xu;Mingjie Li;Zhibing Jiang;Yibo Liao;Yining Chen;Bangyi Tao
title: A multi-decadal, depth-resolved Area-of-Habitat dataset for global marine species
abstract:
Marine species are shifting as the ocean changes, yet global information on suitable habitat through both time and depth remains limited. We created a global dataset for 5,619 marine species across seven years from 1995 to 2025 and 50 ocean depth levels. The results reveal clear differences among depths and long-term changes in suitable habitat, providing a resource for studying marine biodiversity change, climate refuges, and conservation planning. 
 Marine biodiversity is being rapidly redistributed in response to ocean change, yet globally consistent datasets that resolve suitable habitat across both depth and time remain scarce. Here, we present a multi-decadal, depth-resolved Area-of-Habitat (AOH) dataset for a globally distributed subset of marine species assessed by the IUCN Red List. We integrated approximately 45.5 million occurrence records with IUCN expert range maps and physical and biogeochemical ocean reanalysis data spanning 1993–2025. Species-specific MaxEnt models were successfully fitted for 5,619 species primarily fishes (4,815 species), together with reef-forming corals, molluscs, lobsters, marine mammals, marine reptiles, mangroves and seagrasses. The fitted models were projected across 50 standard depth layers for 1995, 2000, 2005, 2010, 2015, 2020 and 2025. Phytoplankton, zooplankton and macroalgae were not included. Model predictions were constrained to the original IUCN ranges to generate continuous, range-constrained estimates of environmental suitability, operationally defined here as marine AOH. The resulting dataset comprises species-level layers and aggregated products resolved by depth and year. Internal consistency assessments showed that predicted suitability was generally higher at species occurrence locations across the evaluated species and depth layers. Independent comparisons with global coral-reef distributions and FishGlob scientific survey observations further supported the ecological plausibility and spatial realism of the resulting AOH estimates.

explanation: 该论文与大气环境遥感技术密切相关，因为它涉及大气表面氨浓度的模拟和排放反演，使用了人工智能技术来提高计算效率，这与空气质量监测和大气成分分析直接相关。
topic_words: ['atmospheric ammonia', 'air quality model', 'emissions inversions', 'artificial intelligence', 'data assimilation']
authors: Michael Sitwell
title: EnsAI: an emulator for atmospheric ammonia ensembles
abstract:
EnsAI is a newly developed artificial intelligence based program for efficiently generating ensembles of atmospheric surface ammonia concentrations that can be used in emissions inversions systems. Ensemble-based data assimilation methods are widely used for assimilation and emissions inversions, but are usually very computationally demanding. Once trained, EnsAI can run thousands of times faster than the physics-based models when run on graphics processing units. 
 Ensemble-based methods for data assimilation and emissions inversions are a popular way to encode flow-dependency within the model error covariance. While most ensemble methods do not require the use of an adjoint model, the need to repeatedly run a geophysical model to generate the ensemble can be a significant computational burden. In this paper, we introduce EnsAI, a new AI-based ensemble generation system for surface ammonia concentrations. When trained on an ensemble for ammonia generated by the GEM-MACH air quality model, it was shown that the ensembles produced by EnsAI can accurately reproduce the meteorology-dependent features of the original ensemble, while generating the ensemble 3300 times faster than the original GEM-MACH ensemble. While EnsAI requires an upfront cost for generating the ensemble used for training, as well as the training itself, the long term computational savings can greatly exceed these initial computational costs. When used in an emissions inversion system, EnsAI produced similar inversion results to those in which the original GEM-MACH ensemble was used while using significantly less computational resources.

explanation: 该论文研究了在地球系统模型E3SMv1中，使用两阶段Rosenbrock求解器提高大气化学积分的计算效率。虽然它主要关注计算方法和模型效率，但涉及大气化学过程（如臭氧和NO2的积分），这与大气环境遥感技术和空气质量监测有间接关系。
authors: Rong-You Chien;Joshua S. Fu
title: Using a two-stage Rosenbrock solver to increase computational efficiency in the DOE's Exascale Earth   System Model version 1 (E3SMv1)
abstract:
We implemented a two-stage Rosenbrock solver (ROS2) in E3SMv1 and evaluated it with two atmospheric chemistry mechanisms. At a 180 s timestep, ROS2 reduced chemistry integration time by ~33% versus the original implicit solver on Cori/KNL CPUs, while maintaining stable one-year simulations and small ozone differences (≤1.03 ppb). Species-dependent differences in ozone, NO, NO2, and OH were small. Results support ROS2 as a lower-cost option, with further convergence and CPU/GPU testing needed. 
 The integration of stiff atmospheric chemical systems is a major computational cost in Earth System Models and poses challenges for numerical stability as chemical complexity and temporal resolution increase. In this study, we implement a semi-implicit two-stage Rosenbrock method (ROS2) in the Energy Exascale Earth System Model version 1 (E3SMv1) and evaluate it as an alternative chemistry time-integration scheme. ROS2 is tested with two interactive chemical mechanisms of substantially different size: chemUCI (60 prognostic species) and trop_strat_mozart_mam4 (155 prognostic species). Numerical experiments include short simulations to quantify computational cost, a box-model timestep-refinement analysis, and one-year integrations to examine numerical stability and solution sensitivity. At the same 180 s chemistry timestep, ROS2 requires approximately 33 % less chemistry integration time than the original iterative implicit solver on the tested Cori/KNL CPU platform. The magnitude of this speedup is configuration dependent. Global-mean surface-ozone differences among the tested configurations are small (≤ 1.03 ppb), and the one-year integrations show no evidence of numerical instability. Spatial and diurnal differences in ozone, NO, NO2, and OH are species- and mechanism-dependent, indicating sensitivity to both timestep and solver formulation rather than a common systematic bias. These results support ROS2 as a lower-cost alternative to the current implicit integrator when E3SM chemistry is operated at short timesteps; additional timestep-refinement tests and benchmarking on contemporary CPU/GPU systems are needed to quantify coupled-model convergence and performance portability.

explanation: 该论文主要研究南中部德国的岩石抬升，涉及地质年代学、地貌演化等，与大气环境遥感技术（如空气质量监测、卫星观测、大气成分分析、气溶胶反演）没有直接关联。
authors: Thomas Bernard;Alexander B. Neely;Christoph Glotzbach;Daniel Peifer;Yanqing Shi;Mirjam Schaller;Alexander R. Beer;Todd A. Ehlers
title: Reconstruction of Rock Uplift in South‐Central Germany Since Late Mesozoic Times
abstract: Rock uplift and denudation act as first‐order controls on geological processes that influence atmospheric and ocean composition, and landscape‐forming processes. However, estimating rock uplift rates remains challenging due to the temporal averaging of rates calculated from individual thermo‐ or geochronologic systems. Here we extract uplift rates in a unified modeling framework by combining landscape evolution with inverse modeling of river profiles and thermo‐geochronologic data. We reconstruct Late Mesozoic to present‐day rock uplift of south‐central Germany, using a data set comprising 17 detrital cosmogenic radionuclide samples and 30 thermochronologic bedrock samples. Inversions reveal high uplift rates from 160 to 80 Ma, followed by a decline from 80 to 20 Ma and renewal of uplift until present‐day. This current uplift event is characterized by increasing uplift toward the west across southern Germany. Our results provide a framework to resolve continuous uplift histories and quantify landscape evolution processes and geodynamic controls on Earth's surface.

explanation: 该论文研究金星磁尾中离子回流的时空分布及其与上游条件的依赖关系，涉及太阳极端紫外辐射和太阳风动力压等大气环境遥感技术相关参数，因此与大气环境遥感技术强相关。

authors: Emmett Shei‐House;Jiawei Gao;Chuanfei Dong;Yoshifumi Futaana;Chi Zhang;Xiaodong Wang;Xinmin Li
title: Spatial Distribution of Return Flows Occurrence in the Venusian Magnetotail and Its Dependence on Upstream Conditions
abstract: Venus‐ward return flow can significantly influence ion escape from Venus and may therefore play an important role in atmospheric evolution. However, the mechanism driving return flow remains under debate. Here, we investigate the occurrence rate and spatial distribution of ion return flows in the Venusian induced magnetotail, and their dependence on solar extreme ultraviolet (EUV) irradiance and solar wind dynamic pressure, using 8.5 years of Venus Express observations. We find that EUV irradiance is the primary controlling factor for return flows of both H+ and O+. Under high EUV conditions, the occurrence of closed magnetic topologies and O+ return flow both increase, particularly in the downtail region. In contrast, H+ return flow occurrence decreases significantly compared with low EUV conditions, corresponding to a decrease in open magnetic field topologies. Our results provide observational evidence for understanding the driving mechanism of return flow at unmagnetized planets.

topic_words: ['nitric oxide', 'nitric acid', 'atmospheric nitrogen oxides', 'organic nitrates', 'airborne measurements']
authors: Ben H. Lee;Felipe D. Lopez‐Hilfiker;Ilana B. Pollack;Carsten Warneke;Steven S. Brown;Ronald C. Cohen;Joel A. Thornton
title: Does the Conversion of Biogenic Organic Nitrates to Nitric Acid Control the Lifetime of Atmospheric Nitrogen Oxides Over the Eastern U.S.?
abstract: Airborne measurements over the Southeast US during the summer of 2013 revealed the evolution of nitrogen oxides and nitric acid that was markedly different from that over the Northeast US during the winter of 2015. We can reconcile the observed trends by invoking nitrogen oxide reservoir species formed under elevated NOx environments that then convert to HNO3. This process may represent a daytime loss pathway of NOx that is faster by many factors than the oxidation of nitrogen dioxide by hydroxyl radicals. We present measurements of a suite of organic nitrates made using online iodide‐ionization time‐of‐flight mass spectrometry and simple box modeling that support their role in controlling the net conversion of NOx to HNO3. Rapid loss of organic nitrates derived from biogenic volatile organic compounds, such as what we infer from this analysis, has significant implications for our understanding of oxidant budgets and top‐down NOx emissions assessments.

explanation: 该论文研究了广岛火灾烟羽的高度，使用了大气折射指数和射线光学方法，这与大气环境遥感技术（如大气成分分析）密切相关。
authors: David M. Romps;Rusen Öktem;Zhenyu He
title: A Lower Bound on the Altitude of the Hiroshima Firestorm Plume From Ray Optics
abstract: Projections of nuclear winter are critically sensitive to the height of soot lofted by firestorms, yet direct observations of firestorm plumes are scarce. Here, a lower bound is established for the height of the Hiroshima firestorm plume 97 min after detonation. This bound is obtained via a ray‐optics calculation using the Enola Gay's flight log, which gives the location and time when the plume was last visible. Profiles of the atmosphere's refractive index are taken from three reanalyses (ERA5, CERA‐20C, and 20CR), and uncertainties in the aircraft's distance, altitude, and the atmospheric profile are propagated via Monte Carlo. With 95% confidence, the firestorm plume top exceeded 11.3 $11.3$ km, which means that soot was lofted well into the upper troposphere, consistent with nuclear‐winter scenarios.

explanation: 该论文研究的是地壳动力学中的残余地形与俯冲板块几何形状的关系，属于地质学研究范畴，与大气环境遥感技术（如空气质量监测、卫星观测、大气成分分析、气溶胶反演）无关。
authors: Yuwei Zhang;Dietmar Müller;Maria Seton
title: Negative Residual Topography in Global Back‐Arc Basins Scales With Slab Dip
abstract: Dynamic topography above subduction zones is widely inferred, but its magnitude and controls remain poorly constrained at the global scale. Here, we estimate residual topography across a range of back‐arc basins by correcting bathymetry for sediment loading, crustal structure, and lithospheric age, and compare the anomalies with slab geometry and subduction parameters. Most basins show negative residual topography, and the anomalies become more negative with increasing slab dip. Continental–oceanic back‐arc basins tend to show more negative residual topography than ocean–ocean systems. Residual topography further covaries with cumulative subducted water content, consistent with a possible influence of hydration‐modified mantle rheology on slab‐driven flow. Although the number of basins with complete slab constraints remains limited, these results suggest that slab geometry is associated with negative residual topography in back‐arc regions and provide observational constraints for geodynamic models of mantle flow around subduction zones.

explanation: 该论文研究了加拿大永久冻土野火排放的挥发性有机化合物（VOCs）及其对空气质量的影响，涉及空气污染监测和大气成分分析，与大气环境遥感技术密切相关。
authors: Xueying Liu;Zejiang Yu;Yifang Ban;Hemraj Bhattarai;Theodore K. Koenig;Lingcao Huang;Enze Zhang;Claire Granier;Guy Brasseur;Zhe Wang;Jimmy C. H. Fung
title: Important but Overlooked Reactive Organic Carbon (ROC) Air Pollution From Permafrost Wildfires in Canada
abstract: Canadian permafrost wildfires, characterized by surface flaming and deep organic soil smoldering, emit complex suites of volatile organic compounds (VOCs). These emissions include air toxics that pose substantial public health risks and fuel secondary pollution, yet remain understudied. We quantified VOC emissions from the record‐setting 2023 wildfires using three inventories (GFED, GFAS, QFED) and assessed air quality impacts via GEOS‐Chem simulations and in situ observations. VOC emissions amount to ∼15 ± 8 TgC, just ∼2% of inorganic carbon. Despite this small fraction, their impacts are significant: simulated concentrations increase by 2–5 μg m−3 for benzene and 5–35 μg m−3 for formaldehyde and acetaldehyde during the fire season. Organic aerosols account for ∼60%–80% of the persistent record‐high PM2.5 during the season. These findings highlight the distinct role of high‐latitude permafrost wildfires in driving regional reactive organic carbon (ROC) pollution and provide a framework to address interdisciplinary Earth science challenges.

explanation: 这项研究主要关注地壳的电阻率成像和地震破裂，与大气环境遥感技术（如空气质量监测、卫星观测、大气成分分析、气溶胶反演）没有直接关系。
authors: Yan Deng;Ji Tang;Xiaobin Chen;Zeyi Dong;Shuai Ruan;Bing Han;Junmeng Zhao;Qiang Xu;Yuhan Xiong;Heng Zhang
title: Three‐Dimensional Resistivity Imaging Constrains Crustal Heterogeneity Beneath the 2010 Yushu Ms 7.1 Earthquake Rupture
abstract: The 2010 Yushu (eastern Tibetan Plateau) Ms 7.1 strike‐slip earthquake ruptured unilaterally toward the southeast but left a hypocentral segment without mapped surface rupture, followed by a two‐stage reorganization of aftershocks. We present a 3‐D electrical resistivity model from 70 quality‐controlled magnetotelluric sites acquired shortly after the event. Alternative data‐component inversions, 2‐D/3‐D comparisons, and anomaly‐focused forward tests identify the best‐resolved features. A conductive mid–lower crust beneath the Qiangtang block abuts more resistive Bayan Har crust. The mainshock and early aftershocks lie near upper‐crustal resistivity transitions, while a broad shallow conductor extends beneath and beyond the hypocentral surface‐rupture gap. The late conjugate swarm extends into a sparsely sampled sector. The underlying electrical structure is therefore not well resolved. The results indicate that crustal heterogeneity may have influenced rupture segmentation and early aftershock redistribution, whereas the relation to the late swarm requires denser observations.

explanation: 该论文研究了北极海冰反照率变化对太阳加热的影响，涉及大气环境中的海冰和太阳辐射，与大气环境遥感技术中的卫星观测和大气成分分析相关。
authors: Ali H. Siddiqui;Christopher Horvat
title: Solar Heating of the Arctic Ocean Driven by Changes to Sea Ice Albedo
abstract: The sea ice albedo feedback is the process by which Arctic warming causes sea ice retreat, which due to the reduction in surface albedo leads to further Arctic warming through increased solar absorption. This definition, however, neglects important associated changes in cloud cover that can mitigate this effect, as well as covariant changes in the albedo of ice‐covered regions. Here we investigate a decomposition of the solar forcing of the Arctic Ocean into ice‐edge, ice‐albedo, and solar forcing related effects. We find that changes to solar heating of the Arctic Ocean are projected to be equally driven by changes to sea ice albedo as they are by the decline of sea ice extent. We show that changes to the parameterization of sea ice surface process and Arctic clouds contribute more to uncertainty in projections of the albedo feedback response than uncertainty in sea ice area loss.

explanation: 该论文研究了深对流和中小尺度重力波之间的相互作用，涉及大气动力学和天气现象，与大气环境遥感技术中的大气成分分析和天气监测密切相关。
authors: Ananya Sen;Michael L. Kaplan;Rajan Bhandari
title: Interplay Between Deep Convection and Mesoscale Gravity Waves
abstract: Although the association between precipitation and mesoscale gravity waves (MGWs) is well documented, the feedback mechanisms governing their amplification remain difficult to isolate. This study uses convection‐permitting numerical simulations with 1–4 km grid spacing to investigate a complex MGW event that occurred over the south‐central United States on 7 March 2008. The waves developed within a recurring synoptic environment characterized by a pronounced pre‐existing baroclinic zone and highly curved jet streak circulation. However, following the onset of deep convection, the wave modes diverged markedly in structure and energetics, demonstrating strong sensitivity to precipitation system. The event transitioned from a moderate‐amplitude, dry MGW of depression MGWD1 $\left({\mathrm{M}\mathrm{G}\mathrm{W}}_{\mathrm{D}1}\right)$ to a high‐amplitude, moist‐wave regime comprising an MGW of elevation MGWEL $\left({\mathrm{M}\mathrm{G}\mathrm{W}}_{\text{EL}}\right)$ and a MGW of depression MGWD2 $\left({\mathrm{M}\mathrm{G}\mathrm{W}}_{\mathrm{D}2}\right)$. It was embedded with a localized mesohigh–wake‐low pressure couplet. Two‐dimensional ray‐tracing and four‐dimensional Lagrangian back‐trajectory analyses demonstrate that differences between the dry and moist wave packets were partly attributable to the direct influence of moist convection on the generation and maintenance of the secondary wave mode and the rapid amplification of the primary wave mode. Comparison of CTRL with a “fake‐dry” experiment, where moist diabatic processes were suppressed, shows that convective thermodynamic forcing and midtropospheric jetlet circulations trigger a secondary wave mode. Nonlinear balance residual and Lagrangian Rossby number diagnostics indicate that MGWD1 $\left({\mathrm{M}\mathrm{G}\mathrm{W}}_{\mathrm{D}1}\right)$ was modulated by upper‐level jet‐imbalance forcing near southeastern Texas before propagating northeastward into Louisiana without further amplification. These results show how multiscale diabatic and dynamical interactions generate localized pressure perturbations and sustain a high‐impact MGW event.

explanation: 该论文研究如何通过环境条件预测低云的出现，涉及云量指数（LCAIs）和云控制因素，这与大气环境遥感技术中的空气质量监测、卫星观测和大气成分分析密切相关。论文中提到的线性与非线性模型（特别是神经网络）用于预测云态，这与遥感技术在云气候反馈中的作用直接相关。
authors: Daeho JIn;Lazaros Oreopoulos;Dongmin Lee;Kyu‐Myong Kim
title: Linear Versus Non‐linear Models in Predicting Low‐Cloud Regime Occurrences From Cloud‐Controlling Factors
abstract: Accurately predicting low‐cloud occurrences from environmental conditions is essential for reducing uncertainties in cloud‐climate feedbacks. This study evaluates linear and non‐linear frameworks—specifically, anomaly‐based ridge regression and neural network (NNet) that predict raw target values—to predict cloud regime occurrence frequencies from low‐cloud‐amount‐indices (LCAIs) and other cloud‐controlling factors at monthly, 4° resolution, using data from selected subtropical study regions. While the combined use of multiple LCAIs notably enhances linear model performance within the training domains, these models exhibit poor geographic transferability due to the diversity of cloud‐environment relationships. In contrast, an NNet model trained using raw physical variables consistently outperforms the linear models and captures established physical mechanisms, such as the capping inversion effect. Nevertheless, global application of the baseline NNet model reveals a “generalization gap,” particularly in extra‐tropical and tropical warm‐pool environments that are not represented in the training data set. To address this limitation, an expanded model is trained using additional samples from poorly predicted regions. This approach substantially reduces regional biases and improves mean absolute error by 30%–50%. However, it also introduces greater nonlinearity and regional trade‐offs, including slightly inferior performance within the original training regions. These findings suggest that, although a generalized cloud‐regime model may be achievable, it requires high‐capacity non‐linear architectures and diverse sampling strategies to address the variable nature of cloud–environment relationships. Once successfully developed, however, such a framework could serve as a computationally efficient alternative to satellite simulators for CR‐based evaluation of Earth System Model outputs.

title: A New Physics‐Constrained Neural Network Approach to Retrieve CH4 Vertical Profiles From Hyperspectral Infrared Data
abstract: Methane (CH4 ${\text{CH}}_{4}$) is a critical greenhouse gas, and accurate monitoring of its vertical distribution is essential for understanding its radiative impact and identifying emission sources. This paper introduces a novel methodology using a physics‐constrained neural network based on soft constraints to retrieve CH4 ${\text{CH}}_{4}$ vertical profiles from hyperspectral Infrared Atmospheric Sounding Interferometer (IASI) data. The methodology combines the advantages of Optimal Estimation and neural networks, leveraging physical constraints to enhance retrieval accuracy while maintaining computational efficiency. The approach integrates dimensionality reduction techniques, such as Principal Component Analysis and Averaging Kernel optimization, to maximize information content while reducing computational complexity. Two models were developed: one for general profile retrieval and another optimized for detecting surface level enhancements. The novel approach was validated on synthetic data and applied to real IASI observations, including the Nord Stream pipeline sabotage event, and demonstrated that the algorithm can confidently detect CH4 ${\text{CH}}_{4}$ enhancements as low as 50 ppbv near the surface and reconstruct profiles with average error of ∼20 ${\sim} 20$ ppbv in the mid‐troposphere and >100 ppbv in the stratosphere on the considered test set. While effective in capturing strong enhancements, the technique exhibits slightly reduced sensitivity near the surface due to limited spectral information, which is mitigated by inflating covariance matrices in the cost function. This methodology offers a promising tool for global CH4 ${\text{CH}}_{4}$ vertical monitoring with existing sensors and could be potentially extended to other compounds such as CO2 ${\text{CO}}_{2}$.

title: Elevation Dependence of Rainfall and Snowfall in Global Mountains: Insights From Reanalysis and Convection‐Permitting Models
abstract: Mountain precipitation varies systematically with elevation—a relationship known as the elevation dependence of precipitation. This dependence governs hydrological partitioning and ecosystem stability in high‐mountain regions worldwide. However, the elevation dependence of precipitation and its underlying physical drivers across global high‐mountain regions remain poorly understood. Here, we use reanalysis data sets and convection‐permitting models (CPMs) to elucidate elevation‐dependent precipitation characteristics across four major high‐mountain regions, including the Tibetan Plateau, the North American Cordillera, the Andes, and the Alps. Our results reveal that along windward slopes across all four regions, precipitation increases with elevation, reaches a maximum at intermediate elevations, and then decreases. Regionally, the precipitation maxima over the Tibetan Plateau and the North American Cordillera are mainly controlled by the topographic contribution, whereas those over the subtropical Andes and the Alps are primarily governed by wind convergence. By contrast, in non‐windward regions, precipitation increases consistently with elevation. Regarding the precipitation phase, snowfall increases with elevation across most areas of the four mountain regions, driven by phase transitions and enhanced precipitation efficiency that together outweigh reduced moisture supply at high altitudes. Rainfall shows similar elevation dependence to total precipitation, but reaches its maximum at lower elevations on windward slopes, reflecting a transition from rainfall to snowfall. CPMs capture these features well, resolving finer vertical precipitation structures over windward slopes and showing stronger elevation dependence in non‐windward regions, with the physical processes responsible for the stronger elevation dependence in ICON varying regionally. These findings improve our understanding of the relationship between topography and precipitation and have important implications for water‐resource management and climate adaptation in mountainous regions worldwide.

title: Satellite‐Based Assessment Reveals Patterns of Coastal Marsh Carbon Sequestration Along the U.S. East and Gulf Coasts
abstract: Coastal marshes are critical blue‐carbon ecosystems, yet regional quantification of vegetation‐derived carbon burial and living biomass carbon stocks within marshes remains limited. Here, we developed a transparent, measurement‐based framework integrating Sentinel‐2 data (2019–2024), field biomass measurements, marsh‐type distribution maps, and literature‐derived marsh‐type‐specific carbon allocation parameters to estimate living biomass carbon stocks and vegetation‐derived burial rates across tidal marshes of the U.S. East and Gulf Coasts. Among tested vegetation indices (VIs), the Green Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (GNDVI) showed the strongest relationship with field‐measured above‐ground biomass (AGB) across seasons and marsh types. Applying the calibrated GNDVI–AGB relationship, we mapped annual peak AGB and used seasonal AGB differences as a satellite proxy for net above‐ground primary production (NAPP). By combining remotely sensed AGB with marsh‐type‐specific allocation strategies, vegetation carbon fractions, and below‐ground burial efficiency, we quantified regional living biomass carbon stocks and vegetation‐derived carbon burial rates. Our results suggest, along the East and Gulf Coasts, mean living biomass carbon of about 832 ± 202 g C m−2, corresponding to a total of 11.1 Tg C, and a mean vegetation‐derived carbon burial rate of 70 ± 47 g C m−2 yr−1, totaling about 0.94 Tg C yr−1. These vegetation‐derived burial rates are comparable to those of seagrass meadows and mangrove forests, demonstrating that coastal marshes function as similarly effective blue‐carbon sinks despite differences in plant structure and productivity. This study demonstrates that remote sensing provides a transparent, scalable, and cost‐effective approach for monitoring blue‐carbon dynamics and informing coastal management strategies.

title: Synergistic Management of Abandoned Cropland Mitigates Trade‐Offs Between Food Security and Climate Mitigation in Hilly and Mountainous Areas
abstract: Abandoned cropland is a crucial strategic reserve to reconcile food security (SDG 2) and climate mitigation (SDG 13). However, maximizing these co‐benefits in ecologically fragile hilly regions is constrained by intense spatial competition between food and carbon. In this study, we proposed a spatial decision‐making framework that integrates suitability assessment and Pareto optimization to quantify trade‐offs and identify synergistic pathways in a typical hilly province of Southwest China. The results showed that although the remaining abandoned cropland had substantial potential for either food (4.0 × 1011 kcal yr−1) or carbon (1.38 × 106 t CO2 yr−1), the dual‐suitability overlap rate reached 69.1%, leading to high opportunity costs under single‐objective management. Crucially, scenario simulations and Pareto analysis identified Pareto‐efficient compromise solutions for balancing regional benefits. When spatial prioritization was combined with intensified management, food and carbon potentials could be increased by 125.0% and 51.6%, respectively, without expanding beyond abandoned cropland. These findings highlight that governing abandoned cropland in complex terrain requires spatially differentiated zoning that distinguishes food‐dominant, carbon‐dominant, and synergistic management zones to achieve regional synergistic gains.

title: Spatiotemporal Propagation and Future Risks of Agricultural Drought in Response to Meteorological Drought Across Asia
abstract: Under the background of global warming, drought risk has intensified. Clarifying the changing patterns and response relationships of different drought types is vital for risk management and climate change adaptation. Using multi‐model data from the Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase VI (CMIP6) and an improved three‐dimensional clustering algorithm, this study identified meteorological and Agricultural drought (AD) events in Asia. We analyzed the spatiotemporal differentiation, migration patterns, and response relationships between the two drought types under different future Socioeconomic Pathways (SSPs). The results showed that, under the historical scenario, AD events outnumbered Meteorological drought (MD) events by 77 occurrences, while their average duration was 0.2 months shorter than that of meteorological droughts. The spatiotemporal correlation between meteorological and AD varied regionally, being strongest in Central Asia and southern East Asia, while weak or negative in North Asia and the Qinghai‐Tibet Plateau. Under future scenarios, from SSP1‐2.6 to SSP5‐8.5 scenario, meteorological droughts exhibited longer duration, and both types showed higher severity. The average duration of MD events increased from 2.3 to 3.9 months, and the average migration distance extended from 1,166.3 km to 2,650.4 km. The proportion of matched pairs in which MD preceded AD rose from 29% under SSP1‐2.6% to 60% under SSP5‐8.5. Under the scenarios of SSP2‐4.5, SSP3‐7.0 and SSP5‐8.5, a model‐derived crossover between the fitted SPEI and SSMI trends occurs around 2058. These findings reveal the complex and transitive nature of future drought risk in Asia and provide a scientific basis for formulating targeted drought‐resistance strategies.

title: Imminent Emergence of Permanent Surface Marine Heatwave States Across Global Oceans
abstract: Marine heatwaves (MHWs) can devastate ocean ecosystems, yet the timing at which anthropogenic changes in MHW characteristics permanently emerge from natural variability at the global scale remains poorly quantified. Here, we present the first global time of emergence analysis of MHW characteristics of the ocean surface using simulations from 21 Earth system models from the sixth Coupled Model Intercomparison Project under moderate (SSP2‐4.5) and high (SSP5‐8.5) greenhouse gas emissions scenarios. Relative to a 1985–2014 baseline, we find that almost 48% of the global ocean has already experienced significant trends in both annual MHW days and frequency. Across tropical oceans, MHW conditions permanently emerge between 2020 and 2040 regardless of emission pathway, indicating that near‐term transformation is unavoidable. By mid‐century, half the global ocean is projected to experience MHW conditions for at least 50% of the year, increasing to 90% by 2100. Regions experiencing the strongest warming show the earliest emergence, with uncertainty in emergence timing comparatively low in the tropics (10–15 years) but expanding substantially at higher latitudes (30 years). These findings demonstrate that persistent, large‐scale marine thermal stress is imminent, demanding transformation from reactive crisis management to anticipatory ocean governance within the next two decades.

title: Climate‐Driven Straightening of Western North Pacific Tropical Cyclone Trajectories
abstract: Tropical cyclone (TC) trajectory shifts remain a critical uncertainty in climate risk assessment. However, due to the absence of effective quantification methods for TC trajectories, our understanding of the overall characteristics of their trajectory shifts and the underlying impact mechanisms remains quite limited. Here, we introduce an important metric, sinuosity, as the parameter to describe the overall trajectory of TCs, and propose a new sinuosity‐based machine learning framework for their classification. The findings reveal a significant decrease in the sinuosity of TC trajectories over the Western North Pacific. This reduction is mainly due to straighter trajectories within the recurving cluster TCs, which follow conventional southeast‐to‐northeast recurving trajectories, with most dissipating in Northeast Asia. This “straightening” phenomenon of recurving TCs is jointly driven by the shortening of TC duration and the westward expansion of the Western Pacific Subtropical High (WPSH). As the trajectories of recurving TCs are becoming straighter, they are more likely to make landfall in Northeast Asia, significantly increasing the regional risks of TCs. These findings unravel a previously unobserved dimension of TC climate response, demonstrating how changes in subtropical circulations are reshaping regional hazard patterns with profound implications for disaster preparedness, mitigation, and adaptation strategies.

title: Diet at disease onset determines tissue inflammatory memory
abstract:
Dietary state during a narrow temporal window can durably reprogram disease trajectory. 
 Obesity, which is often associated with prolonged exposure to an obesogenic diet, substantially alters immunity1–7, but whether brief dietary changes shape acute inflammatory responses and long-term tissue memory remains unclear. Here we show that transient high-fat diet (HFD) exposure at the onset of acute type 17 skin inflammation exacerbates disease in lean mice to levels comparable to those associated with chronic obesity. This effect is restricted to a discrete 4-day peri-initiation window; HFD outside this window has no impact, whereas switching obese mice to a low-fat diet (LFD) during a similar window fully blunts disease amplification. Mechanistically, HFD rapidly recruits neutrophils into the skin, and neutrophils in challenged skin express high levels of Nlrp3 (ref. 8) and Il1b. Neutrophil depletion, genetic Nlrp3 deficiency and pharmacological NLRP3 inhibition each blunt the HFD-induced inflammatory amplification. These findings nominate a neutrophil–NLRP3–IL-1β axis that licences pathogenic IL-1R1+CD4+ T helper type 17 (TH17) cells9,10. After recovery, a chromatin-poised tissue-resident memory T cell population persists. Consequently, mice exposed to HFD at disease onset develop exaggerated inflammation upon recurrence, despite recovery and maintenance on LFD. Transient HFD similarly amplifies lung TH17 inflammation through neutrophil- and IL-1R1-dependent mechanisms. Together, these findings show that dietary state during a narrow temporal window can durably reprogram disease trajectory, suggesting that short-lived physiological states may become embedded in local immune memory11 when they coincide with tissue inflammation. title: Weakened association between sequential phenological events corresponds to interphase extension
abstract:
Seasonal events in temperate deciduous trees, from leaf-out to leaf fall, follow a fixed annual sequence. This study shows that the timing of consecutive events is statistically associated in European trees, but that the association between fruiting and leaf coloration has weakened in some species as the interval between these phases has increased. 
 The sequential occurrence of leaf unfolding, flowering, fruiting, foliar senescence and other life-cycle events constitutes a full cycle of plant phenology. Temporal shifts in the seasonal timing of these phenophases have been regarded as key evidence of global environmental change. Most previous studies, however, have focused on the timing of individual phenophases. Little is known about the relationships between changes in timing across sequential phenophases. Here, using in-situ phenological records of major European tree species between 1980 and 2017, we show strong positive associations between consecutive phenophases. In particular, the statistical relationship between the timing of consecutive phenophases is comparable to that of temperature for spring phenological events and substantially exceeds the relationship with climatic factors for late-season phenological events. However, the associations themselves have shifted across years, with a significant decrease in the association between the timing of fruit ripening and autumnal coloration, corresponding to the largest extension of interphase duration. Current process-based phenological models largely overlook associations between consecutive phenological events and their interplay with climate change, potentially leading to biased projections of phenological changes and ecosystem adaptation to future climate change. Seasonal events in temperate deciduous trees, from leaf-out to leaf fall, follow a fixed annual sequence. This study shows that the timing of consecutive events is statistically associated in European trees, but that the association between fruiting and leaf coloration has weakened in some species as the interval between these phases has increased.

title: Hydrogen-bond-mediated quasi-two-dimensional covalent organic frameworks for ultrahigh gold extraction
abstract:
Covalent organic frameworks are ideal for precious metal recovery but the confinement of binding sites within inner pores often leads to restricted mass transfer and limits extraction capacities. Here, the authors report a quasi-2D topology-directed strategy to construct exposed binding sites for highly efficient gold recovery. 
 Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are ideal for precious metal recovery due to their high surface areas and tunable binding sites. However, the confinement of binding sites within inner pores often leads to restricted mass transfer, resulting in poor site accessibility and limited extraction capacities. Herein, we report a quasi-two-dimensional (quasi-2D) topology-directed strategy to construct exposed binding sites for highly efficient gold recovery. By incorporating outward-pointing hydroxyl groups, the local conformation of the imine-linked skeleton is effectively locked via inter-chain hydrogen bonding (ICHB), which suppresses molecular torsion and promotes ordered assembly of the 1D chains into a quasi-2D crystalline architecture. This structural rigidification creates unobstructed ion-diffusion pathways and maximizes the exposure of active sites for rapid [AuCl4]− capture and reduction. Remarkably, under mild thermal and vibratory stimulation, gold nanoparticles form in situ and aggregate, yielding a high gold extraction capacity of 5082.32 mg g−1. Theoretical calculations demonstrate that ICHB-induced structural planarization creates a cooperative coordination environment and optimizes the energetic landscape for dechlorination, synergistically promoting guest enrichment and interfacial gold reduction. This work establishes a new blueprint for creating COFs with exposed active sites via inter-chain assembly, offering a scalable approach to maximize site accessibility and electron transfer for selective gold capture.
