title: A combinatorial genetics approach reveals limits to redundancy within Plasmodium falciparum invasion ligand families
abstract:
The authors use a genetic approach to explore redundancy within two multigene families important for Plasmodium falciparum invasion of human red blood cells, revealing that not all family members function equivalently. 
 To maintain infection in the human bloodstream, Plasmodium falciparum parasites undergo repeated cycles of invasion of and multiplication inside red blood cells (RBCs). Two protein families, the Erythrocyte binding-like (EBA) and Reticulocyte binding-like (Rh) proteins, are known to play a key role in invasion, mediating early stages of attachment of the P. falciparum merozoite to the host RBC. There is a degree of redundancy within these families, such that disrupting the function of individual EBA/Rh proteins in vitro is not sufficient to prevent invasion. By employing a novel approach to disrupt multiple EBA and Rh genes in combination, we systematically assess functional interdependency across these families for the first time. This analysis, and further characterisation of mutant parasites, reveals that disruption of some pairs of EBA/Rh ligands significantly impacts P. falciparum invasion, whereas others do not. Disruption of PfEBA175 in combination with either PfRh2b or PfRh4 significantly reduces parasite multiplication in vitro, indicating that the remaining EBA/Rh proteins cannot fully compensate for the absence of these three key invasion ligands. title: Framework desymmetrization enables partial pore space partition in metal-organic frameworks
abstract:
Framework desymmetrization enables partial pore-space partition in acs nets, yielding part-pacs as a new pore partition mechanism. Retained open metal sites boost C₂H₂/CO₂ selectivity and productivity. 
 The pore-space-partition (PSP) has been recognized as a powerful strategy for boosting the uptake capacity of small gas molecules and has seen wide application in reticular chemistry. However, the most successful PSP platform—the partitioned-acs (pacs) net—has followed only one pattern since its inception over a decade ago: one partition agent per partition site, with a general formula of [M3O(L1)3](L2). This fully partitioned architecture occupies all metal sites, eliminating open metal sites (OMSs) and compromising selectivity. Herein, we introduce a partial PSP concept accessed through a framework desymmetrization strategy. By replacing traditional high-symmetry D2h ligands with lower-symmetry C2h ligands (e.g., fumaric acid), we introduce structural distortions into the acs network, breaking the uniformity of partition sites and allowing partition agents to occupy only a fraction of available positions. This provides access to a PSP mechanism, namely part-pacs (partially partitioned-acs), with a general formula of [M3O(L1)3](L2)1/3. The part-pacs structures retain high acetylene capacity while exhibiting significantly enhanced selectivity compared to their fully partitioned analogues. Specifically, part-pacs-fum-tpa achieves C2H2/CO2 separation productivity nearly twice that of its full-pacs counterpart (1.92 mol kg−1 vs 0.98 mol kg−1). Framework desymmetrization enables partial pore-space partition in acs nets, yielding part-pacs as a new pore partition mechanism. Retained open metal sites boost C₂H₂/CO₂ selectivity and productivity.

title: Global socio-economic resilience to disasters
abstract:
Disaster risk assessments often overlook how damages affect well-being and recovery across populations. A global analysis now shows that well-being losses from disasters are much higher than asset damages, with the poorest suffering disproportionately. 
 Most disaster risk assessments use asset damages as their central metric, often neglecting distributional impacts and affected people’s coping and recovery capacity. To address this, the concepts of well-being losses and socio-economic resilience—the ability to experience asset damages without a decline in well-being—have been proposed. Here we provide a global picture of well-being losses and socio-economic resilience using microsimulations. Across 132 countries, 1 dollar in damages causes well-being losses equivalent to a 2-dollar uniform national consumption drop. The poorest populations incur only 9% of damages but 33% of well-being losses. A 10% higher gross domestic product per capita is associated with a 1 percentage point resilience increase. Low-income countries experience 72% greater well-being losses per dollar of damages and need 92% longer to recover than high-income countries. Socio-economic and financial interventions can complement asset-focused policies, and targeting low-income populations usually yields higher well-being returns. Our results offer a starting point for a discussion on more comprehensive risk metrics and risk management policies for sustainable development. title: Disentangling the anthropogenic climate change influence on recent hydroclimate whiplash events via multiple nudged model simulations
abstract:
Disentangling the anthropogenic climate change influence on recent hydroclimate whiplash events via multiple nudged model simulations 
 Hydroclimate whiplash describes swings between extremely dry and wet conditions. The magnitude and physical drivers of changes in observed whiplash events under global warming remain poorly understood. Here we quantify thermodynamically-driven changes in whiplash intensity for nine high-impact events using the Standardised Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index and a unique multi-model ensemble of wind-nudged storyline simulations. Anthropogenic climate change accounts for 9% (range across events: −2 to 72%) of the observed whiplash intensity on a weighted average across events, with positive contributions for nearly all events according to the multi-model mean, and all models agreeing on the positive contribution for about two-thirds of the events. This climate change contribution is predominantly driven by a non-linear increase in potential evapotranspiration, which strengthens drying more during the dry than the wet phase. Model uncertainty on the magnitude of the climate change contribution is substantial, with an inter-model spread of 13% on average across the events. These results highlight a climate change imprint on observed whiplash events and the need for multiple nudged datasets to robustly attribute complex events.

abstract:
Microplastic deposition fluxes at Qomolangma Station exceed those at Everest Base Camp, reflecting topographic and anthropogenic differences, with an estimated annual atmospheric input of 56 tons to the Tibetan Plateau above 4000 m, based on year-long monitoring on Mount Everest’s northern slope. 
 The Third Pole receives long-range transported pollutants, yet atmospheric micro- and nanoplastics inputs remain poorly constrained. Here we report year-long monitoring on the northern slope of Mount Everest using dry, wet, and total deposition sampling. Microplastic deposition fluxes at Qomolangma Station (64.0 n m−2 d−1) significantly exceed those at Everest Base Camp (23.0 n m−2 d−1), reflecting topographic and anthropogenic differences. Deposited microplastics are dominated by fragments, mainly polyamide, polyethylene terephthalate, and polyethylene. Nanoplastic concentrations across five representative months are higher at Qomolangma Station than at Everest Base Camp and include polyethylene, polyethylene terephthalate, polyvinyl chloride, and polypropylene. Monsoon periods enhance wet deposition via short-range transport, whereas non-monsoon periods receive long-range continental inputs. Upscaling suggests an annual atmospheric input of 56.4 tons of microplastic to the Tibetan Plateau above 4000 m. These results identify the atmosphere as an efficient pathway for plastic delivery to the Third Pole, with potential ecological risks despite low ambient concentrations. title: Global warming intensifies compound renewable energy droughts
abstract:
Global warming intensifies renewable energy droughts by reducing wind and solar resources, with greater warming leading to more severe renewable energy droughts, as indicated by climate model projections and machine learning analysis. 
 The transition from fossil fuels to renewable energy is essential for mitigating human-induced climate change and achieving climate neutrality, requiring reliable and resilient renewable energy systems. However, global warming is expected to increase the instability of renewable energy resources, particularly during periods of simultaneous low wind and solar power generation, known as renewable energy droughts. Here, we investigate renewable energy droughts globally under 1.5∘, 2∘ and 3∘C global warming levels using CMIP6 multi-model simulations, explicitly capturing their compound nature and the joint dependence between wind and solar resources. Results show that renewable energy droughts intensify progressively with warming, with statistically significant changes in duration, frequency, and intensity affecting 69.4%, 74.0%, and 50.2% of the global land area, respectively, at 3∘C global warming level. Machine learning analysis identifies solar radiation as the dominant driver of renewable energy drought intensification, with influence strengthening under higher global warming levels. These findings highlight the need to integrate compound risk assessments into renewable energy planning to ensure system reliability in a warming world. Global warming intensifies renewable energy droughts by reducing wind and solar resources, with greater warming leading to more severe renewable energy droughts, as indicated by climate model projections and machine learning analysis.

title: A process-based screening framework for coastal reservoirs
abstract:
Reservoir geometries influence freshening while offshore wave statistics poorly proxy nearshore loads, showing that coastal reservoir suitability depends on coupled controls rather than hydrology alone, suggests a process-based screening framework applied to coastal archetypes in Taiwan. 
 Reservoirs underpin global water supply, yet new upland storage is increasingly constrained by topography, ecosystems, and social acceptance. Coastal reservoirs, impounding river discharge in estuaries and lagoons, offer an alternative, but early-stage suitability is shaped by coupled risks from salinity, marine forcing, water quality, and shoreline change. We develop a transferable, process-based screening framework of five screening dimensions and 16 ordinal indicators, with numerical modules (salinity transport, sea-state transformation, morphodynamics) placing all candidate sites on a consistent present-day basis for quantitative comparison. Applied to three coastal archetypes in southern Taiwan, suitability depends on coupled controls rather than hydrology alone: reservoir geometries influence freshening, and offshore wave statistics poorly proxy nearshore loads. Rankings are robust to weighting, and diagnosed weaknesses can be improved by design refinement and re-screening. The framework enables transparent, reproducible cross-site comparison and provides actionable screening criteria to support climate-informed, resilient coastal water-storage planning. abstract:
Extratropical Cyclone Harry produced exceptional impacts in the Central Basin of the Mediterranean in January 2026 through substantial amplification of secondary microseisms, according to a synthesis of multi-disciplinary observations and modelling 
 Between 19 and 22 January 2026, the extratropical Cyclone Harry generated the highest individual wave height ever recorded in the Mediterranean Sea, causing widespread coastal flooding and erosion across the central basin. Here we combine oceanographic and meteorological observations, high-resolution morphodynamic datasets, hydrodynamic modelling, and regional microseism analysis to show that Harry produced the most severe coastal impacts of any Mediterranean cyclone in recent decades. Process-based XBeach and HEC-RAS simulations across 19 coastal sites in Sardinia, Malta, Sicily, and Calabria reveal unprecedented inundation extents strongly modulated by local geomorphology, with submarine canyons, buried palaeo-channels, and urban infrastructure amplifying wave setup and inland flooding. Concurrently, broadband seismic records from 55 Mediterranean stations show exceptional secondary microseism amplification, with Ionian stations reaching the highest amplitudes since the beginning of seismic recordings in 1990. Harry’s Microseism Reduced Amplitude exceeded previous storms and Mediterranean cyclones by more than fourfold, highlighting escalating coastal risk under climate-driven cyclone intensification. title: Slow craton thickening can increase the frequency of kimberlite eruptions
abstract:
A gradual thickening of deep cratonic lithosphere after 1.5 Ga is consistent with, and may help explain, the long-term increase in kimberlite magmatism, according to analysis of numerical models of craton evolution and age distribution of kimberlite eruptions 
 Although cratons are stabilized by their thick and highly viscous lithosphere, their long-term thermal evolution remains poorly understood. Here, kimberlite-hosted mantle xenoliths can provide constraints on past craton thickness, as they erupt almost exclusively beneath thick cratons that protrude into a ‘kimberlite window’ of 160–250 km. Global compilations indicate that kimberlite eruptions become more frequent and continuous after 1500 Ma. Therefore, we link two fundamental questions: how craton thickness evolved through time, and whether this evolution influenced kimberlite magmatism. We present 27 two-dimensional numerical models of craton evolution within a convecting mantle, and explore the effects of initial craton thickness, compositional buoyancy, radiogenic heating, and mantle cooling. Although cratons originated as hot and thick layers in the Archean, gravitational flattening likely thinned them above kimberlite-generating depths. With progressive cooling, craton viscosity and density increased, allowing cratons to undergo gradual thickening after  ~ 2000 Ma. We conclude that thickening processes, such as tectonic compression and cooling, operate faster than thinning processes, such as sub-lithospheric dripping, to slowly thicken cratons into the ‘kimberlite window’. Such thickening is a possible explanation for the increasing frequency of kimberlite eruptions after  ~ 1500 Ma. title: Pervasive patterns in bird songs resemble those in human speech and song and are independent of vocal learning
abstract: Bird songs are often described as analogs to human speech and songs, but expansive comparisons are necessary to determine analogy and mechanistic substrates. By analyzing global corpora consisting of 367 bird species (>74,500 vocal elements from ~5900 songs) within two clades of vocal learners (oscines and hummingbirds) and related nonlearners (suboscines and nightjars) and 52 human languages (>15,000 elements in >800 speech or song phrases), we revealed common patterns in bird songs that resemble prevalent patterns in human speech and song with variation in resemblance to speech or song. Vocal learning did not systematically affect acoustic patterning or similarity to human vocalizations. These data underscore the deep analogies between bird and human vocalizations and convergent motor mechanisms shaping communication.

title: Chiral altermagnon in MnTe
abstract: Altermagnetism has been recognized as a magnetic phase that bridges the properties of ferro- and antiferromagnetism. The momentum-dependent spin splitting observed in these materials reflects their distinctive symmetry characteristics, which also establish the conditions for chiral magnons to emerge. Here we provide direct experimental evidence for a chiral magnon in the altermagnetic candidate manganese telluride (MnTe) revealed by circular-dichroism resonant inelastic x-ray scattering. This mode, which we term chiral altermagnon, exhibits a distinct momentum dependence of its spin polarization consistent with the altermagneticg-wave symmetry of MnTe. Our polarization-resolved data corroborate the existence of a discrete class of magnetic excitations, demonstrating how altermagnetic order shapes spin dynamics and paving the way for advances in spintronic and quantum technologies.

title: Rapid longitudinal flights cause time shifts and Sun compass error
abstract: Many animals use the Sun compass to guide their movement, sometimes over thousands of kilometers. Consistent use of the Sun compass relies on the endogenous clock to track the Sun’s arc, yet animals traveling east-west experience time shifts, potentially causing mismatches between their internal clock and local time. Using GPS, we reveal that Manx shearwaters (Puffinus puffinus) experience such shifts during homing flights, generating predictable errors in Sun compass orientation. Use of the Sun compass persists even when shearwaters have access to compass-independent cues during coast following. Our findings provide a new avenue for chronobiology research in the wild, suggesting that rapid longitudinal movements may affect other processes governed by the endogenous clock and that conserved chronobiological mechanisms impose substantial constraints on navigation.

title: Intrinsic gestational timing governs human cerebellar development after preterm birth
abstract: Intrinsic programs shape brain maturation; however, which of these programs are perturbed by prematurity as well as the molecular pathways involved remain unknown. The human cerebellum serves as a paradigm of extrauterine development—its accelerated growth and circuit formation align with the third trimester, a period disrupted by preterm delivery. Using multimodal datasets encompassing in vivo neuroimaging and neurodevelopmental outcomes with postmortem spatial-transcriptomic and histopathological profiling, we show that prematurity diverts the cerebellar developmental trajectory. Cerebellar growth and functional outcomes scaled with gestational age, despite modifying perinatal exposures. Spatially resolved developmental programs underlying macroscopic trajectories were marked by incomplete granule cell maturation and impaired Purkinje cell structural refinement, which indicate lineage-specific developmental asynchrony. Thus, prematurity constitutes biologically displaced maturation, in which infants of equivalent postmenstrual age occupy divergent developmental states.

title: Stimulated protein degradation to promote mitochondrial function and neuronal survival
abstract: Targeted protein degradation is a promising modality to treat cancer or inflammation, but whether it can provide a similar benefit for disorders caused by pervasive protein dysregulation is unclear. We describe stimulated protein degradation (SPD) as a strategy that leverages agonists of stress-responsive E3 ubiquitin ligases to simultaneously eliminate multiple pathogenic factors. Specifically, we show that activators of the reductive stress response E3 CUL2FEM1Bboost degradation of multiple physiological substrates to improve mitochondrial import and electron transport chain assembly. In this manner, CUL2FEM1Bagonists preserve mitochondrial function and neuronal survival in models of neurodegenerative COX deficiency syndrome and Friedreich’s ataxia. By activating E3 ligases that evolved to safeguard cellular integrity, SPD expands the use of compound-induced protein degradation to complex pathologies of high unmet need.

title: Spatial coordination in the codevelopment of the human urogenital system during organogenesis
abstract: The human urogenital system originates from a common embryonic domain, yet the mechanisms guiding its spatiotemporal coordination remain understudied. Here, we combined high-resolution spatial transcriptomics with single-cell multiomics to profile human embryos from Carnegie stages 15 to 23, capturing the codevelopmental dynamics of the urogenital system. We revealed mesonephros- and adrenal primordium–derived signals that promote gonadal specification and enable efficient in vitro generation of cells resembling early gonadal lineages. We also uncovered a possible mesonephric origin of gonadal supporting cells through rete testis or ovarii linking the mesonephros. Finally, we delineate three transcriptionally distinct steroidogenic lineages differing in cholesterol sourcing, cortisol synthesis, and sex hormone production that together orchestrate sex differentiation. These findings deepen our understanding of urogenital system assembly and guide the exploration of coordinated multiorgan development.

title: A commensally regulated immune rheostat fine-tunes skin barrier fitness
abstract: At the skin’s surface, the epidermis must balance stem cell renewal with barrier maintenance to withstand environmental stress and shield against pathogens. In this study, we identify a microbial-immune-epithelial feedback mechanism that integrates environmental information into stem cell regulation in mice. Specifically, we show that Langerhans cells (LCs), an intraepithelial macrophage population, orchestrate this circuit by producing prostaglandin E2, which restrains stem cell proliferation, promotes epidermal differentiation, and maintains barrier integrity during homeostasis. Upon pathway disruption, stem cells become overactivated, hindering terminal differentiation and weakening barrier function. Upstream, LC activity is tuned by the local microbial environment in a rheostat-like fashion, coupling commensal sensing to stem cell dynamics. Our findings provide a general framework for how barrier tissues achieve adaptive homeostasis amid continual external fluctuations.

title: Western Pacific double subduction drives Gulf of California rifting
abstract: Continental rifting reflects the balance between tectonic forces and lithospheric strength, yet the mechanisms of breakup remain debated. Rapid rifting of the Gulf of California oblique rift (GOCOR) ~6 million to 8 million years ago is a key example; it may have resulted from the lithosphere responding to external kinematics or acceleration of long-lived extension. The dynamics of either scenario remain incompletely understood. In this study, we highlight that the rapid rifting of the GOCOR coincides with the initiation of Western Pacific double subduction. Using three-dimensional geodynamic models, we show that such subduction reorganization can transmit extensional stresses of ~5 to 15 megapascals across the Pacific plate, loading the GOCOR and the southern San Andreas fault. Subduction reorganization may represent the missing driver for the initiation of rapid GOCOR rifting within a preconditioned lithosphere and may be an overlooked tectonic force behind other rifting events.

title: Whole-body single-cell atlas of an adult vertebrate, Danionella cerebrum
abstract: A complete cell type transcriptome atlas of a vertebrate could promote understanding of animal cell type composition, organization, and evolution. The miniaturized, transparent, and regenerative teleostDanionella cerebrumbrings whole-vertebrate single-cell profiling experiments within reach. We performed region-stratified single-cell RNA sequencing across the adultDanionellabody and mapped cell types and gene expression at single-cell resolution using spatial transcriptomics. We delineated spatially distinct neural cell types on the basis of their regional gene expression signatures. The body-wide atlas elucidated cell types harboring adult molecular positional memory, uncovered paedomorphic features, and revealed conserved body-region and appendage-specification programs in adult connective tissue. Comparative analyses revealed conserved neural cell types, and regeneration datasets uncovered expression dynamics during telencephalon regeneration. This whole-vertebrate transcriptome atlas yields a comprehensive resource for myriad questions in biology and neuroscience.

title: Papaver self-incompatibility is controlled by two multiallelic idiomorphs
abstract: Self-incompatibility (SI) prevents self-fertilization through highly polymorphic genetic recognition at theSlocus with multiple alleles. InPapaver rhoeas, theSdeterminants were previously identified asPrpSandPrsS. However, we found thatPrpS-PrsSwas absent in manyShaplotypes. In this work, we report the identification of an alternative pair of polymorphicSgenes,S locus oligopeptide transporter(SOPT) andS locus glycine-rich protein(SGRP), segregating at theSlocus whenPrpS-PrsSis absent.SOPTandSGRPdisplay hallmarkSdeterminant features and confer SI when heterologously expressed inArabidopsis thaliana. Therefore, instead of having allelomorphs with homologous variants, thePapaverSI system is determined by two multiallelic idiomorphs sharing no obvious common ancestry. This discovery of a dual-idiomorph system reveals a distinct genetic basis for polymorphism, with implications for the evolution of allorecognition mechanisms.

title: Data-driven discovery and rapid, direct synthesis of MXenes
abstract: MXenes are a rapidly expanding family of two-dimensional transition metal carbides and nitrides, yet scalable synthesis routes remain limited and historical reports suggest a broader, largely unexplored chemical space. We used machine learning–assisted database mining to uncover hidden multilayer MXenes. Screening reveals 33 previously synthesized but unrecognized MXene candidates. Guided by these findings, we synthesized seven multilayer MXenes using a rapid, scalable self-propagating high-temperature method that requires no sustained external heating and completes within minutes. We further realized 11 previously unexplored rare earth–based MXenes (M = praseodymium, neodymium, samarium, gadolinium, terbium, holmium, and thulium). Experiments and modeling suggest semiconducting behavior and diverse magnetic states across this family. Together, these results expand the MXene family and demonstrate a data-driven strategy for accelerating materials discovery through sustainable methods.

title: Genomic erosion across avifauna in a biodiversity hotspot sounds a conservation alarm
abstract: Loss of biodiversity can have a hidden dimension—the cryptic erosion of genetic diversity even in the face of apparent species resilience. We quantified changes in genetic diversity by comparing historical and modern genomes of 62 songbird species from the Gaoligong Mountains, a biodiversity hotspot in southwestern China. We identified genomic loss averaging between 43 and 49%; and, unexpectedly, common species were disproportionately affected. We argue that this loss was driven primarily by habitat fragmentation (and mitigated by dispersal ability) and show that it exceeds prior estimates and conservation policy thresholds. Species identified as having lost diversity continue to be listed as “Least Concern” on the International Union for Conservation of Nature’s Red List of Threatened Species, exposing a blind spot in extinction risk monitoring. We call for genomic metrics to be rapidly integrated into global conservation frameworks.

title: The delocalized nature of chemical bonding at a catalytic metal surface
abstract: Adsorbate bonding at metal surfaces requires hybridization of localized molecular orbitals with delocalized electronic bands of the metal; hence, the electronic wave function involved in bonding may extend far beyond the adsorption site. We revealed the consequence of this delocalization by determining the distance over which structural variations of the metal surface influence the molecule-metal bond strength. Velocity-resolved kinetics provided adsorption energies for three molecules bound at atomic steps of platinum (Pt), each exhibiting bond-strength changes of up to 0.2 electron volts as the step-step distance varied over 100 angstroms. We observed molecule-specific behavior reflecting the hybridization of molecule-specific orbitals with symmetry-selected orbital bands of the metal that respond differently to structural modifications of the solid. We discuss implications of these observations for adsorption on Pt nanoparticles.

title: In-cell structures visualize human pre-ribosome assembly in the nucleolus
abstract: In eukaryotes, ribosome biogenesis initiates within the nucleolus, a hallmark multilayered compartment of the nucleus. Structures of pre-ribosomes have been characterized ex situ, but their assembly pathways within human nucleoli have not been described. Here, we used cryogenic correlative light and electron tomography to visualize molecular landscapes within HeLa cell nucleoli and obtained in-cell structural snapshots of both ribosomal subunit precursors, the small subunit processome and the pre-60S. These recapitulate major states resolved previously ex situ and reveal additional critical interaction partners, including the RNA exosome, rixosome, and nuclear export receptor CRM1-RanGTP. We further show how pre-ribosome assembly landscapes are altered upon RNA polymerase I inhibition. Our study combines molecular structures with cellular context to elucidate the spatiotemporal assembly pathway of the human ribosome.

title: The global geography of threats to freshwater biodiversity
abstract: Human activities are eroding biodiversity, especially in freshwater systems. Despite major advances in quantifying species vulnerability and threats, we still lack a crucial understanding of where threats are affecting freshwater species globally. Here, we produced a species-centered spatial assessment of threats, mapping the impact of 45 threats across 21,490 freshwater species of amphibians, fish, mammals, odonates, and reptiles. We found that species in highly developed and water-managed regions are strongly affected by multiple overlapping threats. Although threats vary across taxa and regions, increasing threat probabilities elevate extinction risk and population declines, with freshwater species experiencing greater threat intensity and distinct spatial patterns than terrestrial species. Our findings establish a spatially explicit baseline for targeting the most urgently needed freshwater conservation and management interventions.

title: Altermagnetism revealed by polarized neutrons in MnF2
abstract: Altermagnets are compensated magnets with symmetry-enforced spin split bands. Direct spectroscopic evidence for their existence has been reported in several materials. For example, inelastic neutron scattering (INS) has recently been used to witness a splitting of magnon bands in MnTe that is compatible with altermagnetism. Here, we present polarized INS results on MnF2showing that it is altermagnetic. Our data reveal a splitting coming from the long-range dipolar coupling. Furthermore, using a domain-biased sample, the data reveal a nonzero chirality in the neutron scattering cross section that reverses the sign between the two magnon modes. It is this feature that clearly demonstrates altermagnetism in MnF2. This finding highlights the potential for polarized INS to characterize altermagnets through its sensitivity to fine structure in magnon spectra.
